chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has missed days from the month of Ramadan; does he fast voluntarily (before making up the missed days)? He said, 'No, until he makes up what is due to him from the month of Ramadan.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever becomes a junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) in the morning on a day for which he had intended fasting, whether for making up the missed days of Ramadan or for voluntary fasting, his fasting is not valid. This is indicated by what has been narrated:

key_terms.جُنُبًا: In a state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim need to make up missed Ramadan days before fasting voluntarily?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential principle that obligatory fasting (qada) takes precedence over voluntary fasting (ta'taww'), a ruling derived from the Prophet's explicit instruction to Abu al-Subakh al-Kinani. It further clarifies that becoming junub before dawn invalidates the fast for both qada and voluntary days, emphasizing the necessity of resolving major impurity prior to the Fajr call to prayer. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the validity conditions of fasting being tied to the state of purity at the time of the fast's intention and commencement.
